'''Virginie Chamard''' (born 1974){{r|idref}} is a French [[crystallography|crystallographer]] whose research involves the development of methods for [[coherent diffraction imaging]] and [[ptychography|Bragg ptychography]],{{r|tool}} and the use of these methods to understand the crystal structure of [[biomineral]]s, including [[coral]], shell, and mineralizing microorganisms;{{r|silver}} she has also applied her research to [[microelectronics]] and [[nanoelectronics]].{{r|if}} She is a director of research for the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS), affiliated with the [[Fresnel Institute]] in [[Marseille]].{{r|silver}}

Chamard defended her doctoral thesis, ''Études structurales du silicium poreux par techniques de rayons'', in 2000 at [[Joseph Fourier University]], under the direction of Gérard Dolino.{{r|these}} After postdoctoral research at the [[University of Dortmund]] in Germany, she joined CNRS in 2003 and joined the Fresnel Institute in 2008.{{r|if}}

She is a 2026 recipient of the [[CNRS Silver Medal]].{{r|silver|if}}
